items.q: What happened to the Pi harness over the past year?
items.a: Its core **barely changed**, yet it got far more capable **purely because models improved**.

items.q: How has agent run length changed for Armin Ronacher?
items.a: P90 runs went from about **2.5 minutes to 14+ minutes**, which **changes how you work** with a harness.

items.q: What happened to many old prompting tricks and plugins?
items.a: With present-day models they are **no longer necessary**; much of the gain is **emergent model behaviour**.

items.q: What limits agent output now, according to Ronacher?
items.a: **Human attention**: prompts per day stay flat while agent time explodes, and only **10-15 of 141 projects** get maintained.

items.q: What is the true skill when working with agents?
items.a: Knowing **when to push back**, because agents are rewarded for **completing the goal**, not for a coherent design.

items.q: How does Ronacher review work he no longer reads line by line?
items.a: At about **70% of the session** he asks for an **executive summary and a typeset HTML page** before verification.

items.q: Why do open standards matter more with agents?
items.a: Agents make it easy to **reimplement formats**, so versions **diverge**; shared specs and **upstreaming over forking** keep software compatible.

items.q: Why do long-running agents need to be durable?
items.a: So they can **suspend and resume** on their own and wait for cheap **flex-scheduled inference** without wasting sandboxes.
The harness can **orchestrate thousands of tool calls** and cheap **classifier decisions** in code instead of through the context.
